the development of novel algorithms for the design of robots capable of operating in a wide range of real-world environments, with the goal of making robots more robust, reliable and safe.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we present a novel domain adaptation approach that combines a universal controller with a differentiable physics-based online system identification module to improve generalization of the system identification module.
UC-DiffOSi improves the generalization of the domain adaptation module and the universal controller.
we present a novel approach to online system identification for robots that leverages prior knowledge in the form of a differentiable physics simulator.
The main takeaway from our work is that

UC-DiffOSi can learn a more generalizable identification module than existing methods, and that the identification module can improve the generalization of the UC to novel environments, even when the environments have different physical properties than the environments the UC was trained on.
combining UC with differentiable physics engines can significantly improve the performance of online system identification.
UC-DiffOSi is a simple yet effective approach to combine domain randomization and domain adaptation.
